main_text.p: & doctrinam pertinere ad acquirendam felicitatem: Aristot.cap. 9.
Sic Rom.1.16: Evangelium potentia Dei. Et 10. 17. Fides ex auditu: Matt.7.7: Petite & dabitur vobis.
Convenient. VIII. Esse stabile & immutabile quiddam, μονιμόν[?], καὶ μηδαμῶς ἀμετάβολον: Aristoteles cap.10.
Sic Ioh.10.28. Nemo rapiet oves meas, &c. 2. Ti-moth.2.19: Solidum stat fundamentum Dei, &c.
TRANSITIO ad discrepantias, in quibus doctrina Ecclesiæ approbetur: & defectus philosophiæ ostendantur.
Discrepantia I. In scientia Architectonica, quæ philosophis est politica: Ecclesiæ Scriptura Sacra seu Theologia.
Approbetur sententia Ecclesiæ per antithesin, ostenso philosophiæ defectu.
I. Quia non Politica, sed sola Scriptura sacra tradat veram cognitionem Dei, perfectissimi boni: Deut.4.6.Ioh.1.18: Deum nemo vidit unquam, &c.
II. Quia ipsa Politica subserviat Scripturæ tanquam nobiliori.
Ostendatur applicatione duorum argumentorum Aristotelis, quibus primatum vendicat politicæ, ad Scripturam.
I. Quod hæc accuratissime docent, quæ artes & scientiæ discendæ, & in Republ. admittendæ sint, vel non sint. Rom.12. v.3.6.&c. Deut.8.10. 1.Cor.7.10.1.Thess.4.11.

page.notes: The Greek word μονιμόν is uncertain and marked. The running head's "HEOLOG." is partly worn, and the initial letter may be T. The Greek in the Aristotle line is copied from the scan and could be checked. No marginal notes are printed. Show-through from the facing page is ignored.
